options.description: Asks with plain lines in and lines out rather than a region that redraws, for a screen reader: the question is written once, what is typed is echoed where it is typed, and nothing already written is ever moved or erased.
options.name: accessible

options.description: Whether Escape leaves the prompt to go back a step. Defaults to `false`, where Escape does nothing, as it always has.
options.name: back

options.description: Returned when the answer is empty. Shown dimmed in the empty field.
options.name: default

options.description: Accept fractions. Defaults to `false`, so the answer is an `int` by the parser's own rules and no decimal point can be typed.
options.name: float

options.description: What the field starts with, editable. Unlike `default`, it is not a fallback.
options.name: initial

options.description: The largest answer. Up stops here, and Enter above it is an error.
options.name: max

options.description: The smallest answer. Down stops here, and Enter below it is an error. A `min` of zero or more is also what stops a `-` being typed.
options.name: min

options.description: Shown dimmed when nothing has been typed, in place of `default`.
options.name: placeholder

options.description: The input router to read keys through. One is built if not given.
options.name: router

options.description: Gives the prompt up when this aborts, the way Ctrl-C does.
options.name: signal

options.description: Where keys come from. Defaults to the terminal's input.
options.name: stdin

options.description: How far Up and Down move. Defaults to `1`.
options.name: step

options.description: Checks the answer, after the range has. Return a string to reject it with that message, or anything falsy to accept.
options.name: validate
options.type: (value: number) => string | undefined | false | Promise<string | undefined | false>

options.description: An answer to start from: the field opens holding it, as it does `initial`, which it beats. One the field could not hold -- not finite, or a fraction without `float` -- is dropped rather than refused, leaving `initial`. One out of range is kept, and Enter says so, as it does for an `initial`.
options.name: value

registryDescription: A number prompt: min, max, step, and arrows that change the value
